minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Mayor Pachota opened the public hearing.\par
\par
Clerk Michaels read the ordinance only.\par
\par
Communications were provided in advance.\par
\par
Planner Brittany Smith provided a presentation to include the request, general information, project description, aerial map, existing and proposed conditions, future land use map, proposed future land use map, zoning map, site photo, surrounding land uses, planning analysis, comprehensive plan consistency, land development code compliance, conclusions and findings of fact, and answered Council question regarding future land use enclaves and stated it has annexed into the City and still has County zoning designation, high density residential, uses being similar, and current zoning allowances. \par
\par
Planning and Zoning Director Clark noted density is being reduced, it is a new proposed land use, and building height being addressed in the rezone application.\par
\par
City Attorney Fernandez stated Council needs to consider if they are comfortable with the portion not currently mixed use corridor (MUC) becoming MUC versus remaining high density residential. \par
\par
Discussion took place on future land use, the code, mixed use corridor, height, and zoning. \par
\par
Marty Black, Agent for Applicant, provided a presentation to include site aerial map, surrounding area, future land use and zoning, noting the current Sarasota County zoning, existing development standards, proposed development standards, graphic representation, buffer graphic, proposed binding stipulations, and answered Council questions regarding development of a hotel on the front and multi-family or accessory uses in the back, total land area, entitlements, high density residential, and how standards should be applied. \par
\par
Discussion continued regarding the stipulations in the rezoning ordinance, if approved, and only being changed if a request was approved by Council. \par
\par
David Gress, 825 Guild Drive, expressed concerns about proposed zoning changes especially LU-1, residents being disturbed, and property values.\par
\par
Liz Gifford, 709 Guild Drive, spoke on preferring high density residential over multi-use/hotel, and changes since the applicant workshop.\par
\par
Mayor Pachota closed the public hearing.\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Discussion took place regarding Community Development Block Grant (CBDG) funding for affordable housing, and the Bayshore Drive sidewalk project future. \par
\par
Recess was taken from 2:23 p.m. to 2:30 p.m. \par
\par
Discussion continued regarding the joint meeting with Sarasota County, the hospital on the Island, The Venice Theatre rebuild and funding, evacuation centers, affordable housing, and homelessness. \par
\par
City Manager Lavallee thanked Village on the Isle Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Doug Foeller for the organization's hospitality.\par
\par
Ms. Steiner provided a review of the discussion and recommendations:\par
\par
\pard\fi-360\li720\cf0\f1\'b7\tab\f2 Regarding Seaboard, we have direction that the council is eager for to see visual progress and while we know certainly that there is work that must happen to move facilities before there can be streetscaping there is an eagerness to see progress visually. \par
\pard\par
\pard\fi-360\li720\f1\'b7\tab\f2 There was also support from the Council to pursue the opportunity for a swing bridge at the Seaboard area. \par
\pard\par
\pard\fi-360\li720\f1\'b7\tab\f2 Regarding the Venice Community Center, the direction was to start with potentially an outside vendor by using an RFP process to identify opportunities with an outside vendor as the first choice. If that was not successful, the second choice would be to identify an in-house solution with city run staffing and operations. \par
\pard\par
\pard\fi-360\li720\f1\'b7\tab\f2 The other part of that discussion focused on the sentiment to not lose money or to at least break even and to look at opportunities to generate a profitable revenue growth path.\par
\pard\par
\pard\fi-360\li720\f1\'b7\tab\f2 It was highlighted that we want to make sure there is public input into the Parks planning process from our citizens. \par
\pard\par
\pard\fi-360\li720\f1\'b7\tab\f2 The \ldblquote Vanbulance\rdblquote Fleet received accolades and hopes that that continues to be part of our emergency response going forward.\par
\pard\par
\pard\fi-360\li720\f1\'b7\tab\f2 There was an interest in what possibilities there might be to obtain improvement of the flood rating and staff recognized that there was some priority, though it might be challenging to increase to the next level.\par
\pard\par
\pard\fi-360\li720\f1\'b7\tab\f2 The issue of Flamingo ditch was raised and a sense of urgency around funding opportunities was expressed as it relates to a meeting coming up on the 19th of February. \par
\pard\par
\pard\fi-360\li720\f1\'b7\tab\f2 It was discussed that beach parking is also a priority and that the topic will be an item for consideration with the agenda at the forthcoming meeting with the county.\par
\pard\par
\pard\fi-360\li720\f1\'b7\tab\f2 Another issue that may go on the agenda relates to the county trees along Airport Road that were lost or damaged due to recent hurricanes. \par
\pard\par
\pard\fi-360\li720\f1\'b7\tab\f2 There is interest in exploring or doing a pension review to determine if there is a significant cost or whether to assess the pension situation for an opportunity to buy them out with the first step being what the cost would be to review that situation. \par
\pard\par
\pard\fi-360\li720\f1\'b7\tab\f2 There was support for Finance to consider the current CIP Threshold Policy to raise the dollar levels needed for approval and authorization through the CIP process. \par
\pard\par
\pard\fi-360\li720\f1\'b7\tab\f2 The topic of affordable housing was raised. Particularly knowing that in the future, there may be opportunities with city property related to Seaboard and Legacy Park and that of property that is contiguous to the current Housing Authority properties at Venetian Walk. \par
\pard\par
\pard\fi-360\li720\f1\'b7\tab\f2 Interest in the Bayshore Drive safety issue relating to a sidewalk project.\cf1\f0\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Stormwater Engineer Steve Behrens provided a recent history of the storms in Venice, flooding in the Flamingo Ditch area, and introduced the consulting firm Coastal Protection Engineering (CPE). \par
\par
Tom Pierro, PE, DCE, presented a progress update of the Flamingo Ditch Feasibility Study, including the study overview, model and data review, public comment summary, preliminary findings, and next steps. \par
\par
Captain Joe Morrow, PE, commented on the Interconnected Pond and Channel Routing (ICPR) Model development, updates, and refinements. \par
\par
Michelle Pfeiffer, PE, spoke on the public comment period, and citizens' concerns. \par
\par
Mr. Pierro summarized the preliminary findings, flooding, two-fold challenge, stormwater drainage, storm surge inundation, potential concepts to improve the system, long-term plan to improve drainage, short-term actions with potential strategies, and next steps.\par
\par
Discussion took place on previous drainage structure, funding, eligibility for grants, backflow devices, storm surge, short-term options, and long-term solutions.\par
\par
Mayor Pachota summarized the City will receive a more definitive report this summer, CPE will work with City staff on short-term solutions before coming back with long-term solutions, and will work with staff on grant opportunities.\par
\par
Mr. Pierro noted the summary was correct and emphasized that in terms of seeing construction, in addition to ownership issues, funding issues, and grant issues, the regulatory component will be a major factor and permitting issues with the various agencies can take years.\par
\par
Discussion continued on urgency, importance of getting solutions right, Elevate Florida and FEMA programs, and construction easements.\par
\par
City Manager Lavallee commented on the grant process, and asked the consultant if they could work within this scope. \par
\par
Mr. Pierro stated they could assist with the narrative for grants if the City meets eligibility components and answered Council questions regarding whether they have encountered private ownership of a drainage system before, and whether there were other solutions beyond Flamingo Ditch to address the drainage issues of the Golden Beach area. He noted the situation was unusual, and is similar to New Orleans physically due to the bowl-like terrain, and whatever solutions are implemented it must be ensured they are not an obstacle for future planning. \par
}

action_text: A motion was made by Ms. Farrell, seconded by Mr. Smith, that based on the Evidence in the Record, City Council deny Petition No. 22-40SP on the basis that the petition is not consistent with the comprehensive plan and is not in compliance with the Land Development Code because 1) it violates Land Development Regulation (LDR) Sec. 86-23(m), the site plan is inadequate in automotive and pedestrian safety, and 2) it violates LDR Sec. 86-23(m)(6) stormwater standards promulgated 30 years ago do not protect properties today, the Southwest Florida Water Management District (SWFWMD) is reviewing the antiquated rules. The failure to provide floodplain compensation to offset the filling in of the pond at Jacaranda and Laurel puts residents at risk, and 3) Sec. 86-23(m)(2) is violated and a narrow definition of intensity Floor Area Ratio (FAR) was utilized even if the LDR is not specific it should have considered a wider interpretation of intensity to include traffic, lighting, hours of operation, the size of the parking lot, and the effects of the adjacent properties.

\par
Frank Domingo, PE, Stantec, being duly sworn, provided testimony regarding the traffic signal, addressed comments, and Sarasota County's denial of a traffic signal.\par
\par

\par

\par

\par

\par

\par

\par
Mr. Leins responded to Council questions regarding the rainfall criteria, exceeding current City criteria, drainage concerns of neighbors, and watershed models.\par
\par
Appellant Scott asked Mr. Leins about the calculations, impervious surface, ponds, and wetlands.\par
\par

\par
Jennifer Menendez, PE, being duly sworn, and Gary Scott presented the appellant case SWFWMD permit documents, the model of rain and runoff, downstream, errors in modeling, existing and proposed conditions, discrepancies, peaking factor, impervious area, flooding issues, recommended the City have an engineer look at this complex model to ensure accuracy, and estimated the cost of 20 hours for the review at $5,000 to $10,000. \par
\par
Appellant Scott questioned Mr. Domingo about his communication with Sarasota County, users of the proposed shopping center, safety, intersection, conflict points, total traffic interconnection patterns, existing intersection conditions, and capacity.\par
\par
Planning & Zoning Director Clark responded to Appellant Scott's question regarding the best time to review compatibility, and the commercial uses regarding PUD rezoning. \par
\par
City Attorney Fernandez commented that Council can determine relevancy, compatibility, intensity and effect on nearby properties.\par
\par
Ms. Menendez answered Council questions regarding models used, criteria, data, Interconnected Pond and Channel Routing (ICPR) modeling experience, the pond, wetlands, road widening, impervious surface, and SWFWMD.\par
\line Attorney Boone asked Ms. Menendez about the SWFWMD permit, and whether there was an error in issuing the permit, difference between engineers, permitting process, review time and cost estimate, estimate of time for review, and communication with the applicant engineers. \par
\par
Attorney Boone questioned Mr. Domingo on the need for a traffic signal, standards, examples of other unsignalized intersections that are similar and approved for safety.\par

\par
Clerk Michaels read the ordinance by title only.\par
\par
Written communications were provided in advance.\par
\par
Senior Planner Nicole Tremblay provided a review of the proposed Comprehensive Plan Amendment, showing the strikethrough underline text. \par
\par
Attorney Jeffery Boone, Agent for Applicant, commented on the second reading process and requested the opportunity to provide response after public comment.\par
\par
Dennis Johnson, 177 Field Avenue East, spoke on traffic impacts on Field Avenue and Avenido del Circo. \par
\par
Sharon Baum, 111 Nokomis Avenue South, spoke on historic preservation, density, traffic, and safety. \par
\par
Joan Iacono, 1132 Bird Bay Way, spoke on behalf of Venice Thrives, regarding the Comprehensive Plan, and expressed concerns about increased density.\par
\par
Richard Huttner, 960 Cooper Street, spoke on the Comprehensive Plan, and against increased density.\par
\par
Steven Ulrey, 960 Cooper Street, spoke against the increased density, and expressed concerns regarding traffic.\par
\par
David Polley, 960 Cooper Street, spoke against the increased density and in favor of following the Comprehensive Plan.\par
\par
Mary De Armey, 4 Gulf Manor Drive, spoke against the increased density and expressed concerns regarding traffic, and potential strains on utilities. \par
\par
Recess was taken from 10:50 a.m. to 11:00 a.m.\par
\par
Planning and Zoning Director Clark noted this is an entitlement public hearing, does not approve any development, and a complete traffic study would be handled during site and development plan.\par
\par
Attorney Boone provided the applicant response, stating there were no issues from the State after first reading, responded to an audience document regarding traffic, the site and development plan process, public comment, Venice Thrives, the current rights of the property, reduction in commercial development availability, density of developments on the island, John Nolen's plan, traffic engineer's letter, floor-to-area ratio, reduction in traffic in this proposal, and requested approval. \par
\par
Mayor Pachota closed the public hearing. \par

\pard\cf1\fs24 City Attorney Fernandez provided an introduction and history of the petition. \par
\par
Attorney Mark Bentley, serving in the role of mediator, via Zoom, answered Council questions regarding the process.\par
\par
Senior Planner Nicole Tremblay, reviewed the terms of the agreement, Density and Unit Limits, Operational Interconnection, Land Uses, Height, Lot Detail Standards, Signage Standards, Height Exception Application Progress, and answered Council questions regarding density.\par
\par
City Attorney Fernandez commented on density uses in the Planned Unit Development (PUD).\par
\par
Senior Planner Tremblay reviewed PUDs in the area and answered Council questions regarding the PUD, number of units and density, the date of the original application, and open space. \par
\par
Pat Neal, Applicant, spoke on the history of Neal Communities, their relationship with the City, and showed a map of Vistera.\par
\par
Attorney Jeffery Boone, Agent for Applicant, spoke to density, the Florida Land Use and Environmental Dispute Resolution Act (FLUEDRA) process, the order of denial, compatibility, and density. \par
\par
Jim Collins, Agent for Applicant, presented the definition of compatibility, and reviewed surrounding densities.\par
\par
Attorney Boone, further addressed Compatibility Decision Criteria, Common Review procedures, Application Requirements, Planned District Zoning Amendments application requirements, unified control, the three reasons for denial, court proceedings, density, PUDs, and answered Council questions regarding density, concessions, the proposed agreement, stipulations, and possible height exceptions.\par
\par
Mr. Neal answered a Council question regarding changing market dynamics, and the impact of the hospital.\par
\par
Mr. Collins showed map and answered Council question regarding building height in the area, \par
\par
Attorney Boone responded to Council questions regarding the agreement, density, height, number of reduction in density. \par
\par
Recess was taken from 3:13 p.m. to 3:30 p.m.\par
\par
Olen Thomas, 248 Acerno Drive, spoke against the mediated settlement agreement, and commented on compromise, and unified control.\par
\par
Joan Iacono, 1132 Bird Bay Way, spoke on behalf of Venice Thrives, against the mediated settlement agreement and stated there is a lack of plan for the future of Venice. \par
\par
Steve Carr, 149 Avens Drive, spoke on behalf of the Central Venice Coalition, concern about height exceptions, and wording in the document. \par
\par
Attorney Boone responded to questions from Council regarding 12/09/2021 was the date of the Vistera map.\par
\par
Mr. Collins responded to an earlier question regarding density in GCCF PUD, and stated it was originally approved for 1,799 dwelling units. \par
\par
Attorney Boone responded to public concerns, current PUD allows request of up to 55 feet in height, protecting existing SF development to the south and to the east. \par
\par
John Neal, Applicant, stated Council has approved ALF units, needs of the city and residents.\par
}

\par

\par

\par

\par

\par

\par
Mayor Pachota closed the public hearing.\par

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 City Engineer Jon Kramer commented on the project and goal, feasibility study to reduce flooding in Flamingo Ditch, and Coastal Protection Engineering's (CPE) final presentation. \par
\par
Recess taken from 9:53 a.m. to 10 a.m.\par
\par
City Manager Clinch commented on participation in the project, the history of the project, the final presentation not being the final discussion, and actionable items after the presentation. \par
\par
Thomas Pierro, PE, BC.CE, Senior Project Manager and Project Manager, CPE, spoke on study objectives, appreciative of public comments received, historical aerial image of Flamingo Ditch, models, preliminary study findings, workshop follow-up, and additional retention ponds by the airport. \par
\par
Joseph Morrow, PE, Senior Coastal Engineer, CPE, spoke regarding airport retention pond option, Harbor Drive stormwater pipe, removing existing connection to Flamingo Ditch, adding new on-way pipe under Harbor Drive to Deertown gully, overland flow weirs retained in model to allow excess street flow from Harbor Drive and San Marco Blvd to flow towards Flamingo Ditch, and final alternatives 8A through 8D rainfall scenarios, and results summary.\par
\par
Mr. Pierro reviewed recommended actions, grant applications, real-time water level monitoring, storage in Lot 2, pipe improvements, elevate, diverting, surge barrier, conceptual construction cost estimates, study completion, and final deliverables.\par
\par
City Engineer Kramer indicated city engineering staff will prepare a Capital Improvement Program (CIP) project to implement recommendations within budget without increasing stormwater rates, and without compromising the level of service for rest of the city residents. He highlighted grant opportunities the City has pursued, have not received funding at this time, but do have stormwater funding, and the ability to purchase the easement on Lot 2, excavate it, and install a real time water monitoring system. To implement additional recommendations would require additional funding. \par
\par
Discussion followed regarding rationale for proposed pipe size, standardization of culvert size at private properties, available stormwater funding, pipe improvements at multiple locations, changes in elevation of road heights, road elevations and storage, swales, Lot 2 storage, high frequency rain events, pumping, pressurized pipe, pipe size, water location and maintenance, request for funding, alternatives provided, and liability on the City.\par
\par
City Attorney Fernandez commented on improvements as it relates to the City's liability and responsibility on maintaining the stormwater infrastructure. \par
\par
Discussion continued regarding project funding, stormwater master planning, Council and resident participation and involvement as process continues, models, surge barrier issues, diverting water to Deertown Gully, funding sources, and ongoing maintenance of stormwater drainage systems.\par
\par
City Engineer Kramer spoke on stormwater maintenance and current activities, and real time water monitoring level system.\par
\par
Luanne Wood, 550 West Flamingo Drive, spoke on impact to neighborhood, happy with recent action, preference for ditch clean out and being proactive, and in favor of easement purchase of Lot 2.\par
\par
Jimmy Clifford, 908 Villas Drive, expressed concerns about erosion.\par
\par
Rick Magee, 628 Gardenia Drive, spoke on City's obligation to maintain ditch, desire for the City to be more proactive, past flooding issues, and real time sensors.\par
\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Mayor Pachota opened the public hearing and announced this is a quasi-judicial hearing. \par
\par
Deputy Clerk Barcia read the ordinance by title only. \par
\par
\cf0 City Attorney Fernandez questioned Council Members concerning conflicts of interest. There were none. Council Members disclosed ex-parte communications. \par
\cf1\par
Mr. Engelke disclosed attendance at the Planning Commission meeting and a site visit.\par
\par
Mr. Smith disclosed viewing the Planning Commission meeting.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Boldt disclosed attending the Planning Commission meeting and a conversation with Toscana Isles resident Sue Perry regarding what is on the agenda. \par
\par
Mayor Pachota and Mr. Howard disclosed a site visit and viewing of the Planning Commission meeting.\par
\par
City Attorney Fernandez introduced the nature of quasi-judicial proceedings.\par
\par
Written communications were provided in advance.\par
\par
Senior Planner Tremblay, being duly sworn, presented the application, general information, project description, concept plan, proposed connectivity plan, proposed townhome standards, aerial map, existing conditions, site photographs, northern parcel, southern parcel, future land use map, zoning map, surrounding land uses, planning analysis and consistency with the Comprehensive Plan, conclusions and findings of fact, compliance with the Land Development Code, decision criteria, there being no recommendation for approval from the Planning Commission, responded to a Council question regarding the differences between multi-family and townhomes, and displayed the decision criteria for Council to review. \par
\par
Josh Law, Pape-Dawson, Agent for Applicant, being duly sworn, presented a general overview, concept plan, Toscana Isles overview, unified control, background on Toscana Isles, Planned Unit Development (PUD) development standards, Toscana Isles Subareas, Subarea 3, compatibility, development standards, residential street and connectivity standards, and proposed access points.\par
\par
Michael Yates, Palm Traffic, being duly sworn, spoke on the access points and not being able to use Knights Trail due to connection spacing standards, and having legal access to Gene Green Road. He noted Nokomis Groves has access to Gene Green Road.\par
\par
Mr. Law stated the concept plan is to allow for townhomes, and amend connectivity standards map for access to Gene Green Road.\par
\par
Kari MacNutt, Monarch Ecology, being duly sworn, spoke on the environmental issues of the site, wetlands, wetland determination from SWFWMD approved in 2024, historic aerial imagery, drainage conveyance, existing weir structure, wetland impact, mitigation bank, wildlife species, and heritage trees.\par
\par
Matt Morris, Pape-Dawson, being duly sworn, spoke on the master drainage plan, decision criteria, additional criteria for major Planned Unit Development (PUD) amendments, conclusion, requested approval, and answered a Council question regarding access to Gene Green Road.\par
\par
Mr. Yates, responded to a Council question regarding traffic, stating the applicant is providing as much separation from the intersection as possible, and necessary improvements would be dealt with by all who access Gene Green Road. He responded to Council questions regarding private roads, previous litigation regarding access point at Villoresi Boulevard/Knights Trail, and drainage responsibility on Gene Green Road.\par
\par
Discussion took place regarding the easement on Gene Green Road, access points, and Nokomis Groves.\par
\par
Mr. Yates responded to a Council question regarding legal access and Mr. Law displayed an easement and title insurance document.\par
\par
Mr. Morris responded to a question regarding drainage issues. \par
\par
Discussion took place regarding the access point and separation points off of Knights Trail in both directions, drainage, culverts, water flow, and weir.\par
\par
City Attorney Fernandez stated drainage issues are not part of what is being considered today; the focus is on townhomes and the access point on Gene Green Road. She noted other issues are more appropriate for a site and development petition.\par
\par
Discussion continued regarding access points and the applicant being able to apply for a variance from the County regarding Knights Trail, and concerns about the easement on Gene Green Road.\par
\par
Mr. Yates spoke on the variance process with Sarasota County which is decided by the Sarasota County Engineer, access rights based on the easement, and a design exception likely being denied due to the availability of the easement. \par
\par
Discussion continued regarding variance, drainage, and projected rainfall data. \par
\par
Recess was taken from 12:35 p.m. to 2:10 p.m.\par

\par

action_text: A motion was made by Vice Mayor Boldt, seconded by Mr. Engelke, to approve the Revised Mediated Settlement Agreement.
minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Mayor Pachota opened the public hearing. \par
\par
City Attorney Fernandez introduced the Florida Land Use and Environmental Dispute Resolution Act (FLUEDRA) process and history, previous denial and reasons, the special magistrate process, and today's procedures.\par
\par
Special Magistrate Mark Bentley provided an overview of the FLUEDRA, his role as a mediator and hearing officer, and reviewed credentials, the law, options, and implications. Florida Statutes, compatibility, if there is not a settlement today, litigation, options available to Council, reasonable compromise, and encouraged the City to adopt the proposed settlement. \par
\par
Senior Planner Nicole Tremblay presented the history of the proposed Planned Unit Development (PUD) amendment, density and unit limits proposed, optional interconnection, height, lot detail standards, signage standards, height and number of units have changed only, and answered Council questions regarding processes, height exception, change in uses, number of units, and height.\par
\par
Planning and Zoning Director Roger Clark commented that lower heights near the street were proposed by the applicant, and answered Council questions regarding density, heights, acreage, and compatibility. \par
\par
Discussion took place regarding surrounding neighborhoods, density, and nearby heights.\par
\par
Jeffrey Boone, Agent for Applicant, spoke on the corporate entities who own the property, introduced the owners, and his team.\par
\par
Pat Neal, Applicant, spoke on his experience building in the City of Venice, and Florida, finishing the project without further conflict, would like to build an Assisted Living Facility (ALF), standards of law, disclosures. \par
\par
John Neal, Applicant, spoke on the community, complexity of zoning, disclosures, ratio of one to five, showed the disclosures (handouts), mediation requested support of the compromise. \par
Jim Collins, Agent for Applicant, spoke on compatibility components.\par
\par
Jeff Boone spoke on compatibility, the applicant's compromise, and noted the height request being lowered for the Assisted Living Facility (ALF), Independent Living Facility (ILF), and memory care facilities. \par
\par
Pat Neal answered a Council question regarding correspondence received, density, and disclosures.\par
\par
John Neal stated Phase II has not changed at all.\par
\par
Jeff Boone spoke on the original application, the concession offered, and responded to Council questions, regarding previous density, affordable housing, and multi-family housing.\par
\par
Recess was taken from 10:29 a.m. to 10:40 a.m. \par
\par
Mary Sue Bunting, 1078 Ancora Boulevard, Willow Chase, spoke on appreciation for City Council, balance, compliance with City code, density, intensity, and compatibility.\par
\par
Olen Thomas, 248 Acerno Drive, Milano, expressed concerns on the revised mediation process.\par
\par
Joan Farrell, 617 Tamiami Trail North, read a guest column from the Herald Tribune regarding development and developers, and spoke on environmental stewardship.\par
\par
George Davis, 121 Castile Street, Island resident, Venice Thrives, spoke on land use exceptions, height, density, land development code, and lack of compatibility.\par
\par
Joan Iacono, 1132 Bird Bay Way, Venice Thrives, spoke against the mediated settlement agreement, incompatibility, and the best interest of the City. \par
\par
Robin Brugess, 1033 Ancora Boulevard, Willow Chase, spoke against the increase, density, and height. \par
\par
Diana Watters, 273 Mestre Place, VGRC, spoke on the City's vision statement, traffic, and density.\par
\par
Jane Kaveney, 1059 Ancora Boulevard, Willow Chase, expressed concerns on height and density, and against the agreement.\par
\par
Sue Perry, 227 Toscavilla Boulevard, spoke on aging in place, and support for the agreement. \par
\par
Planning and Zoning Director Clark spoke on density in the Vistera PUD, and open space.\par
\par
Jeff Boone commented on the statutory process, one-half the land never being developed, and this not being the same settlement proposal. \par
\par
City Attorney Fernandez responded to a Council question regarding compatibility in regards to the law, density, additional information from the denial process.\par
\par
Mayor Pachota closed the public hearing.\par
}

action_text: A motion was made by Vice Mayor Boldt, seconded by Mr. Engelke, to accept the City Administration's decision to change the work schedules of certain employees to the 5/8 schedule and that no further action be taken to address the impact of the City's exercise of its management right.
attachments: AFSCME Exhibit - 2024 Work in America Survey
Impasse Hearing Procedures Letter from Attorney Fernandez
minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Mayor Pachota opened the public hearing.\par
\par
City Attorney Fernandez provided an introduction to the procedures. \par
\par
Lisa Burke, representative for American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees (AFSCME), presented schedule variations, research statistics on studies showing preferences, revenue, production, employee satisfaction, and reasons, lower absenteeism, higher morale, improved task completions, and competitive work week.\par
\par
Dan Tucci, AFSCME President, presented a weekly schedule planner, side jobs, and the employee financial burden of a 5/8 schedule.\par
\par
Ms. Burke stated there is a financial benefit to the City, and adequate staff coverage.\par
\par
Mr. Tucci stated some employees were hired under the 4/10 schedule planning their life around it, and answered Council questions regarding whether the union was consulted before the change, employee satisfaction surveys, employee comments, employee loss, the weekly schedule planner shown, airport crew, number of employees impacted by the change, whether there are any other proposed solutions, and days of the week impacted.\par
\par
Attorney Mark Leavitt encouraged Council to focus on the issue at hand, management's right to operate the department, the proposed schedule not being a new compromise, impact pay offering during bargaining being declined, studies provided are not City or Florida studies, 21 people affected today, 150 other people in the bargaining unit, only 4% of country is on a 4/10 schedule, and the City trying this schedule previously.\par
\par
Public Works Director Ricky Simpson, stated the scheduling change was in preparation for the Interlocal Parks Agreement changes, began implementing the schedule in March 2025, realignment providing full staff five days per week, improved service to residents and visitors, support for volunteer groups, reduction in overtime cost, and answered Council questions regarding the proposed schedule, five day coverage, bargaining financial wages, any employee satisfaction surveys before and after this issue, and this being one year of evaluation. \par
\par
Discussion took place on holiday pay, acknowledgement of reducing overtime cost of $74,000, the best interest of the city, employee morale, differences in reporting, employee satisfaction surveys, and impasse being declared by the union. \par
\par
City Manager Clinch noted this issue is constantly being re-evaluated, the change coming from the outside, and being based on operational needs. \par
\par
Mayor Pachota closed the public hearing. \par
}
title: Impasse Hearing Between the City of Venice and AFSCME Regarding Shift Schedule Changes

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Discussion took place regarding a Gondolier article, a shift in activity at airport, supporting the airport concerns from the public regarding noise, exhaust, air quality resulting from prolonged Auxiliary Power Units (APUs) use. \par
It was noted the City has control on the ground, but not in the sky. \par
\par
Discussion continued on environmental studies, Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) requirements.\par
\par
City Manager Clinch spoke on the City's experience with environmentally sensitive operations. The City is fully compliant with all regulations, and the master plan will include an environmental analysis, if further studies are needed the City will complete them. He stated the master plan is a long term plan for the future; it does not authorize any projects or expansion. The administration terminal building and t-hangar expansion are the only projects in progress right now, which require their own environmental reviews. The Master plan will help lay the framework for the future, and the consultant's environmental team will be at the meetings in November.\par
\par
Discussion took place on the current plan being outdated, a lot of information at once, not building a commercial airport, public input being helpful, feasibility of a conservation grant to preserve the open space (golf course), noise studies, Fly Friendly program, resident concerns, history of airport and City, and not supporting a commercial airport.\par
\par
Mr. Weed offered a possible amendment which was then rescinded and handled as a separate motion. \par
\par

action_text: A motion was made by Mayor Pachota, seconded by Mr. Smith, to direct the appropriate charter officer to engage the public with the new technical plan as they see fit, pursue demolitions and marketability of the parcels, return to Council with proposed code and architectural standards for the Seaboard Core, and to engage in preliminary discussions with West Coast Inland Navigation District (WCIND) regarding the marina and swing bridge.
minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Mayor Pachota announced the executive session would be moved to 11:00 or 11:30 a.m., there would be a break for lunch, and then the Venice Police Department staffing study would be presented at 1 p.m.\par
\par
Planning and Zoning Director Roger Clark introduced the progression of the Seaboard Technical Plan and the consultant. \par
\par
Josh Frank, Consultant, Dover, Kohl & Partners, presented the Seaboard Phase One Technical Plan schedule, views of Seaboard, Phase One Focus Area, existing conditions, Nolen Street, new intersection, initial phase, private redevelopment, Nolen Street extension, Seaboard redesign, marina improvements, current code, suggested revisions, Focus Area 1, Live/Work Units, examples of projects, Live/Work Units, Rowhouse Units, Seaboard Avenue right-of-way, Seaboard Avenue rendering, Nolen Street right-of-way, Block 1, draft counts, Seaboard Basin, and summary of key project principles. \par
\par
Mr. Frank responded to Council questions regarding the zoning area, building heights, the swing bridge, style standards, outdoor amphitheater, marina space, current businesses in Seaboard, City Code changes, architectural style, and City-owned property. \par
\par
Discussion took place regarding the architectural style, adaptive reuse, keeping the project moving by letting the market drive it, focus on improvement, principles, fundamentals, private development, Sarasota County and other agency involvement, Venice's uniqueness, the marina, heights, the pace of change, and community involvement. \par
\par
Planning and Zoning Director Clark stated Nolen Street is the priority, stepping back from the northern Italian style, offering a seamless style highlighting the history of the area.\par
\par
Discussion took place on redesigning, demolishing, the City Code, remediating, encouraging the staff to involve the Citizen Advisory Board (CAB), conducting another community workshop, keeping an appropriate pace, producing a fact sheet, reaching out to local groups, history, the Venice Historic Precedent (VHP), and West Coast Inland Navigation District's (WCIND's) recommendation of a swing bridge.\par
\par
City Manager Clinch summarized that architectural standards will be revisited, staff will pursue community engagement during season, the property being prepared for potential partnership in the future, making it marketable, and pursing partnerships.\par
}
title: Josh Frank, Consultant, Dover, Kohl & Partners: Seaboard Phase 1 Technical Plan (30 min.)
PRESENTATION WITH ACTION - ITEM CONTINUED FROM THE JUNE 23, 2026 CITY COUNCIL MEETING AND IS SCHEDULED FOR 2:00 P.M.

attachments: Venice Police Department Staffing Study Report
minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Dr. Jones and Dr. May presented on updates since the report, reviewed the reorganization and related positions as well as the financial aspects, analyzing the Deputy Chief position, and peer practice.\par
\par
Chief Andy Leisenring responded to the Council regarding the strain on positions, and the benefit of having a South County jail. \par
\par
Dr. Jones continued on professional standards lieutenant, corporal tier, Side A/Side B, Special operations, recruiting and retention, and answered Council question regarding the increased attrition rate, 5-8 year mark is nationwide, burn out, camaraderie, and community relationships. \par
\par
City Manager Clinch spoke to a small number leaving for financial issues.\par
\par
Dr. May spoke to take home radius policy, extending the mileage radius, payroll and scheduling systems, and answered Council questions regarding the administrative and overtime issues, expediting hiring, payroll systems, and analysis of take home car radius by neighboring counties. \par
\par
Discussion took place regarding payroll systems citywide. \par
\par
Dr. May continued on communications and technology redundancy, increase sworn patrol strength, mutual aid agreement standards, police mutual aid takes effect when requested.\par
\par
Chief Leisenring responded regarding mutal aid, future calls for specific areas, and false alarms.\par
\par
Dr. Jones responded to allocating calls and response, growth, volunteers, and traffic control.\par
\par
Dr. May continued on technology, and drones.\par
\par
Discussion took place on reserve officers, volunteers, off-duty details, retired officers, and professional standards lieutenant.\par
\par
Recess was taken from 2:15 p.m to 2:25 p.m.\par
\par
Dr. Jones commented on Wal-Mart locations outside of the City borders on CAD service log being due to Shop with a Cop events.\par
\par
Dr. May discussed the positioning of officers, and answered Council questions about future evaluation of staffing, and sworn patrol officer growth. \par
\par
City Manager Clinch spoke on this establishing the target. \par
\par
Discussion took place regarding conducting an internal reassessment annually. \par
\par
Dr. May continued on investigations, Venice's caseload being higher than average, expanding civilian staff, directed patrols, vacation watch, seasonal and event-driven loads, community-outreach and co-response functions, 2025 CAD Data, suspicious-person calls, disorder calls, canine program assessment, and answered Council questions regarding canine programs.\par
\par
Chief Leisenring concluded on the results of the study, requested approval for the organizational changes, implementing the things that do not have a fiscal impact for FY27, and moving forward in FY28.\par
\par
There was no public comment. \par
}
